standard_prerequisites.name: Stability
standard_prerequisites.statement: A theory is stable when over every model the number of types in one variable is at most the cardinality of the model raised to the power omega.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the conclusion of the statement.

standard_prerequisites.name: Type over a model
standard_prerequisites.statement: A type is a consistent set of formulas in one free variable with parameters in the model.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is what the proof counts.

standard_prerequisites.name: Isomorphism type of a countable tuple
standard_prerequisites.statement: Countable tuples over a model are classified up to partial isomorphism by their quantifier-free type in the language of the partial structure.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the invariant that bounds the number of types.

core_obligations: Count the one-types over a model M and show that their number is at most the cardinality of M raised to omega, working inside the monster model (source line 1035).

Bound the number of one-types by the number of partial isomorphism types of countable tuples over M, using the results that identify elementarity with the preservation of the partial structure (source lines 1035-1036).
Conclude, since the number of such isomorphism types of countable tuples is clearly at most the cardinality raised to omega (source line 1036).

proof_roadmap.step: Set up the count of one-types over a model.
Bound the count by the number of isomorphism types of countable tuples.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author's labelled proposition at source lines 1033-1034: the theory of free Steiner triple systems is stable. The proof (source lines 1035-1037) is a counting argument, and its substance is the choice of invariant: one has to know that a one-type over a model is determined by the partial isomorphism type of a countable tuple, which is exactly the content of the preceding elementarity results, and only then does the bound by the cardinality raised to omega become immediate. The statement records stability and neither the invariant nor the bounding step.
